project.objective: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico, and what were his exact birth date and place?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico, and what was his exact birth date and place?
questions.rationale: This is the central objective restated as a single researchable question. A birth or baptismal record from the parish(es) serving the Nueva Italia / Parácuaro area of Michoacán — or from Guerrero, given that three confirmed siblings were born in Coahuayutla, Guerrero between 1913 and 1918 — would name the parents and supply the exact event details. Civil registration (registro civil) in Michoacán was generally functional by the 1900s–1910s; parish registers for the area may predate civil records. The siblings' Guerrero birthplaces raise the possibility that Mauro too was born in Guerrero rather than Michoacán, making records from both states candidates. No sources have been searched yet.

items.jurisdiction: Coahuayutla de José María Izazaga, Guerrero, Mexico
items.rationale: The three siblings (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) are documented as born in Coahuayutla, Guerrero, 1913–1918. Their Catholic baptism records in FS collection 1823323 (Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, 1576–1979, name-searchable (personCount 21256598)) will name both parents. Per Mexican naming convention (Mexico_Naming_Customs wiki; loc_001; loc_002), baptism entries record the father's full two-surname name and the mother's full two-surname name — giving us both the paternal-line Cruz surname chain and the maternal Corona surname chain. Searching surname 'Cruz' filtered to Coahuayutla, 1908–1920, should surface all three siblings and potentially Mauro himself if born in Guerrero. This is the required FAN/sibling item for a parentage question and the highest-probability starting point. Per loc_002, the statewide collection is name-searchable and more complete than the San Agustín parish standalone catalog (1037615, browse-only). Also try variant 'Crus.'

items.jurisdiction: Coahuayutla de José María Izazaga, Guerrero, Mexico
items.rationale: Search FS collection 1918291 (Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, 1860–1996, name-searchable (personCount 8406443)) for civil birth registrations of the Cruz siblings and Mauro himself in Coahuayutla, Guerrero, 1905–1920. Civil birth acts (actas de nacimiento) name both parents with full surnames. Per loc_002, compliance dropped sharply during the Revolution (1910–1920), so church records (pli_001) are sequenced first. Mauro may also appear here if born in Guerrero rather than Michoacán. Quirk: the Coahuayutla municipal civil catalog begins only in 1921 (loc_002); use the statewide Guerrero collection 1918291, not the municipal catalog.

Dedicated parentage plan item: search FS collection 1823323 (Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, name-searchable (personCount 21256598)) for the Catholic marriage of a Cruz man to a Corona woman in Guerrero, ca. 1895–1912. This record: (a) confirms the couple as a married unit; (b) supplies the mother's full name — given name + paternal surname 'Corona' + her own maternal surname — which census and death records almost never give; (c) by date relative to Mauro's ca. 1910 birth, corroborates a father named only by the sibling baptisms. Note: the marriage record proves the couple married but is not by itself evidence that Mauro is their child; that link requires a baptism or civil birth record placing Mauro with these parents. Date window: upper bound set by Mauro's ca. 1910 birth; lower bound ca. 1895, assuming parents born ca. 1875–1880 and marrying in their late teens.

The search is no longer necessary to answer q_001.

items.rationale: Search FS collection 1918291 (Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, name-searchable (personCount 8406443)) for the civil marriage of a Cruz man to a Corona woman in Guerrero, ca. 1895–1912. Civil marriage acts often name both parties' parents, supply each party's age, and record the exact date and place. Date window bounded by: parents must have married before Mauro's ca. 1910 birth (upper bound 1910); lower bound ca. 1895 assuming late-teen or early-twenties marriage. Fallback for pli_003 if the church marriage record is not found or not indexed.

items.rationale: Search FS collection 1883388 (Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996) for Mauro Cruz's baptism in Parácuaro, Michoacán, ca. 1907–1913. Per loc_001, Nueva Italia (founded ca. 1909) fell under Parácuaro jurisdiction for this period — Múgica municipality was not created until 1942. Availability: collections_search returned 0 for Michoacán (possible tool-scope limitation); loc_001 confirms this collection covers the target period with images. Search under Parácuaro as the predecessor jurisdiction. A baptism record names both parents and confirms Mauro's exact birth date and place, directly answering both parts of q_001. Also try 'Crus.' If the indexed search underdelivers, the Parácuaro Asunción parish catalog (162793, 1838–1967) is available for a browse-only follow-up.

The premise that he was born near Nueva Italia, Michoacán is invalidated. Replaced by pli_010.

Civil registration compliance was reduced during the Revolution (1910–1920), so this item is sequenced after the church record search (pli_005). The civil birth act (acta de nacimiento) names both parents and records exact birth date and place — directly answering both parts of q_001. Fallback from pli_005 if the church baptism is not found.

items.rationale: Search the 1930 Mexico National Census (Ancestry collection 1771) for Mauro Cruz Corona and his parents. In 1930, Mauro would be approximately 20 years old and may reside in the parental household in Coahuayutla or the Parácuaro area, directly confirming the parent-child relationship. Even if Mauro has moved, parents may appear with younger Cruz children. The 1930 census is the only major Mexican national census publicly available for this era. Ages and birthplaces in the census help confirm identity across records. Date window is a single census year; the window's bounds are set by the census date itself.
items.skip_reason: The 1930 Mexico census would have corroborated the parent-child relationship in the household, but q_001 is definitively answered by the original civil birth registration (src_005) together with four corroborating records. The census cannot add to or change what is directly established by Acta 201.

items.rationale: Full-text co-occurrence search (execute via search-full-text skill) for 'Cruz' AND 'Corona' as separate required terms, run unscoped across FamilySearch's AI-transcribed documents for Guerrero and Michoacán. Per Mexico Naming Customs wiki: a child's baptism entry names the father as '[given name] Cruz [paternal surname]' and the mother as '[given name] Corona [paternal surname]' — the co-occurrence of both family surnames in a paragraph-style entry is a high-precision signal for Mauro's family unit. Surfaces transcription variants and partially-indexed records that defeat name-indexed searches. Deploy as a fallback when indexed searches (pli_001 through pli_006) have been exhausted without finding Mauro's baptism or the parents' marriage.
items.skip_reason: Full-text co-occurrence fallback for pli_005, which was skipped as premise_invalidated (Mauro was born in Guerrero, not Michoacán). The primary search path succeeded: civil birth registration found directly via pli_002/pli_010 searches. Full-text fallback not needed.

items.rationale: Browse the Archdiocese of Michoacán ecclesiastical marriage investigation records (FamilySearch Catalog item 320251, 1637–1915) for the parents' marriage in the Parácuaro area. Per loc_001: 'Archdiocese of Michoacán ecclesiastical marriage investigation records (1637–1915) are at FamilySearch Catalog (catalog/320251) and may document parents' or grandparents' marriages predating civil registration.' These pre-sacramental investigation files (informaciones matrimoniales) routinely name both parties' parents, making them equivalent to a birth record for establishing grandparents' names. Collection ends 1915, covering the parents' likely marriage window. Date window bounded by: parents likely born ca. 1875 and marrying in their late teens or early twenties, making 1895–1910 the core window; upper bound extended to 1915 (collection end). Fallback for pli_003 if the Guerrero church marriage search fails and the parents married in Michoacán rather than Guerrero.
items.skip_reason: Fallback for pli_003 (Archdiocese of Michoacán ecclesiastical marriage). pli_003 is now skipped as 'answered' because the civil birth registration establishes the parents directly. The Michoacán ecclesiastical marriage fallback is therefore not triggered.

jurisdictions.name: Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacan, Mexico

collections.title: Mexico, Michoacán and Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996

quirks: The municipality of Múgica was not created until February 12, 1942. For the 1905–1915 period, Nueva Italia (founded ca. 1909) fell under predecessor jurisdiction — most likely Parácuaro or La Huacana. Search the statewide civil collection under Parácuaro, not Múgica.

No civil registration, church, or census records are available online for the municipality of Múgica per the FamilySearch Wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/M%C3%BAgica,_Infiernillo,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Mexico_Genealogy).
Parácuaro parish (Asunción, 1838–1967) and civil registration (1881–1931) are available at FamilySearch Catalog and are the closest documented records to Nueva Italia for this period.

Civil registration in Mexico began nationally in 1859 but was not strictly enforced until 1867; compliance dropped sharply during the Revolution (1910–1920). Church records are often more complete for this window.

The family was mobile across the Michoacán-Guerrero border. Because the siblings were born in Coahuayutla, Guerrero, search both states' collections simultaneously — Mauro may also have been born in Guerrero.

Mexican naming system: children take the father's first surname and the mother's first surname. 'Cruz' is the paternal surname; 'Corona' is the maternal surname. Index searches should prioritize 'Cruz' as the family name.

Archdiocese of Michoacán ecclesiastical marriage investigation records (1637–1915) are at FamilySearch Catalog (catalog/320251) and may document parents' or grandparents' marriages predating civil registration.

jurisdictions.name: Coahuayutla de José María Izazaga, Guerrero, Mexico

quirks: The Coahuayutla municipal civil registration catalog item begins only in 1921 (FamilySearch Catalog 819525). For the 1913–1918 sibling births, search the statewide Guerrero civil collection (FS collection 1918291, indexed + images) and browse under Coahuayutla.

San Agustín parish, Coahuayutla, recorded baptisms, marriages, and deaths 1819–1930 (FamilySearch Catalog 1037615). This is the primary church source for the 1905–1918 window; browse-only (not name-indexed as a standalone item).
The statewide Guerrero Catholic Church Records (FS collection 1823323) IS name-indexed and may include Coahuayutla San Agustín records — search by surname 'Cruz' in Coahuayutla first.
Civil registration compliance dropped sharply during the Revolution (1910–1920). For sibling births 1913–1918 specifically, church baptismal records are likely more complete than civil records.

Guerrero borders Michoacán to the north and west. The Cruz family was mobile across this border. Search La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca (Guerrero, adjacent coastal municipality) and Parácuaro (Michoacán) alongside Coahuayutla.

The FamilySearch Wiki for Guerrero Catholic Church Records notes: when a person cannot be found, 'consider looking at collections for surrounding localities — Michoacán is to the northwest' (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Guerrero,_Catholic_Church_Records_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records).
Guerrero population ca. 1910: approximately 594,300 (Populstat). State capital: Chilpancingo de los Bravo. Guerrero admitted as state October 27, 1849.
